project.name: Tribora Agent-First Transformation
project.description: Transform Tribora from SaaS-with-AI into an agent-first Knowledge Intelligence Layer. Adds persistent agent memory, autonomous knowledge curation, gap intelligence, contextual AI, onboarding agents, workflow replay, MCP server, and usage-based pricing infrastructure. Builds on existing knowledge graph, agentic retrieval, visual intelligence, and bidirectional sync.

epics.name: Agent Foundation
epics.description: Agent memory system, agent session tracking, agent activity logging, and org-level agent configuration. Foundation layer that all other agent features depend on.

epics.name: Smart Content Processing
epics.description: Auto-generated titles and descriptions from transcripts via Gemini, related content suggestions using knowledge graph concepts, and smart metadata for untitled uploads.

epics.name: Contextual AI
epics.description: Embeddable chat widget scoped to individual content items. Makes RAG capability discoverable on every content detail page without navigating to the assistant.

epics.name: Knowledge Curator Agent
epics.description: Background agent that auto-categorizes content, detects duplicates and near-duplicates, tracks staleness, and suggests merges for overlapping content. Runs periodically per org.

epics.name: Knowledge Gap Intelligence
epics.description: Mines search logs and chat queries to detect knowledge gaps — topics the team asks about but where insufficient or outdated content exists. Includes bus factor analysis and proactive alerts.

epics.name: Agent Authorization
epics.description: Permission tiers governing what agents do autonomously vs. what requires notification or approval. Org-level settings for enabling/disabling agents and controlling autonomy levels.

epics.name: Onboarding Agent
epics.description: Auto-generates personalized learning paths for new team members using knowledge graph and content library. Tracks engagement and adapts paths based on behavioral data.

epics.name: Agent Feedback & Memory
epics.description: Feedback collection on agent actions (thumbs up/down, corrections), concept editing UI, and integration of feedback into agent memory for behavior refinement.

epics.name: Weekly Knowledge Digest
epics.description: Scheduled agent that generates weekly org knowledge reports: new content, trending concepts, knowledge gaps, and health scores. Delivered in-app and optionally via email.

epics.name: Workflow Replay Agent
epics.description: Extracts reproducible step-by-step workflows from screen recordings using visual intelligence (frame extraction, OCR, UI state transitions). Creates living procedure library.

epics.name: Agent Dashboard & Observability
epics.description: Agent activity feed, action detail views, goal-setting UI, status summary widgets, and audit trail export. Makes agent behavior visible and controllable.

epics.name: MCP Knowledge Server
epics.description: Expose Tribora knowledge graph, search, and content as an MCP server. Allows external AI agents (Cursor, Claude, custom) to query organizational knowledge.

epics.name: Pricing & Usage Tracking
epics.description: AI credit consumption tracking, agent action metering, usage dashboards, plan tier gates for agent features, and usage alerts.

stories.title: Create agent_memory table migration
stories.description: As a developer, I want an agent_memory table so that agents can persist learnings, decisions, and context across sessions with embedding-based retrieval.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration creates `agent_memory` table via Supabase MCP (project: clpatptmumyasbypvmun) with columns: id (uuid PK DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()), org_id (text NOT NULL), agent_type (text NOT NULL), memory_key (text NOT NULL), memory_value (text NOT NULL), embedding (vector(1536)), importance (real DEFAULT 0.5 CHECK importance >= 0 AND importance <= 1), access_count (integer DEFAULT 0), last_accessed_at (timestamptz), expires_at (timestamptz), metadata (jsonb DEFAULT '{}'), created_at (timestamptz DEFAULT now()), updated_at (timestamptz DEFAULT now())
Composite unique constraint on (org_id, agent_type, memory_key)

Indexes: idx_agent_memory_org_agent (org_id, agent_type), idx_agent_memory_org_key (org_id, memory_key), idx_agent_memory_embedding using ivfflat (embedding vector_cosine_ops) WITH (lists = 100), idx_agent_memory_importance (org_id, importance DESC), idx_agent_memory_expires (expires_at) WHERE expires_at IS NOT NULL
RLS enabled: SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE where org_id matches authenticated user's org (use service role for worker operations)
update_updated_at trigger applied to agent_memory
Migration applied successfully via Supabase MCP
Typecheck passes

Example: INSERT INTO agent_memory (org_id, agent_type, memory_key, memory_value, importance) VALUES ('org_abc', 'curator', 'tag_vocab', 'react,deploy,setup', 0.7) succeeds and returns the row with generated id and timestamps
Edge case: Attempting to insert a duplicate (org_id, agent_type, memory_key) upserts the existing row rather than failing with a unique constraint violation
Edge case: Inserting a row with importance outside 0–1 range (e.g., 1.5 or -0.1) is rejected by the CHECK constraint
stories.notes: System context: Foundation table for all agent features. Used by US-004 (agent-memory.ts service), consumed by E04 (Curator stores curation decisions), E05 (Gap Intelligence stores analysis history), E07 (Onboarding Agent stores learning path refinements), E08 (feedback integration writes corrections), E09 (Digest stores report templates). The embedding column enables semantic memory retrieval using the same pgvector infrastructure as transcript_chunks. Importance score enables memory decay — less important memories can be pruned. The 1536 dimension matches existing Gemini embedding dimensions used in transcript_chunks.

update_updated_at trigger applied

stories.title: Implement agent memory service
stories.description: As a developer, I want a reusable agent memory service so that all agents can read, write, and semantically search persistent memory with importance-based decay.
acceptanceCriteria: lib/services/agent-memory.ts exists with the following exports:

- storeMemory(params: { orgId, agentType, key, value, importance?, metadata?, expiresAt? }): Promise<AgentMemory> — upserts memory by (org_id, agent_type, memory_key), generates embedding via Gemini embedding model (same as lib/services/embeddings-google.ts pattern), stores in agent_memory table
- recallMemory(params: { orgId, agentType, key }): Promise<AgentMemory | null> — exact key lookup, increments access_count and updates last_accessed_at

- searchMemory(params: { orgId, agentType, query, limit?, minImportance? }): Promise<AgentMemory[]> — semantic search using embedding similarity (cosine distance on agent_memory.embedding), filters by org_id + agent_type + importance >= minImportance, returns top N by similarity
- deleteMemory(params: { orgId, agentType, key }): Promise<void> — hard delete by key
- pruneExpiredMemories(orgId: string): Promise<number> — deletes where expires_at < now(), returns count deleted
- getAgentMemories(params: { orgId, agentType, limit?, offset? }): Promise<AgentMemory[]> — paginated list ordered by importance DESC then updated_at DESC
AgentMemory interface exported with fields matching agent_memory table columns
Uses lazy initialization pattern for Supabase admin client (consistent with lib/supabase/admin.ts pattern)
Uses Gemini embedding model for embedding generation (consistent with lib/services/embeddings-google.ts)
All database operations use Supabase admin client (service role) since this runs in worker context
Typecheck passes

Example: storeMemory({ orgId: 'org_abc', agentType: 'curator', key: 'tag_vocab', value: 'react,deploy,k8s', importance: 0.8 }) generates an embedding via Gemini and upserts the row; calling recallMemory with the same key returns the stored value with access_count incremented to 1
Edge case: searchMemory with a query that has no semantic matches returns an empty array, not an error
Edge case: pruneExpiredMemories called on an org with no expired memories returns 0 and does not error
Edge case: storeMemory with an empty value string is accepted (agents may store empty strings as tombstones)
stories.notes: System context: Core service used by every agent feature. E04 Curator calls storeMemory to remember curation decisions (e.g., 'I categorized recording X as deployment tutorial'). E05 Gap Intelligence calls searchMemory to check if a gap was previously identified. E07 Onboarding calls getAgentMemories to retrieve past learning path decisions. E08 Feedback writes corrections via storeMemory. Follow the lazy initialization pattern from lib/supabase/admin.ts to avoid Railway build failures. Use the same Gemini embedding approach as embeddings-google.ts (model: 'text-embedding-004', 1536 dimensions). Key file references: lib/supabase/admin.ts for lazy Supabase client init, lib/services/embeddings-google.ts for Gemini embedding generation pattern.

stories.title: Implement agent activity logger service
stories.description: As a developer, I want a structured logging service for agent actions so that all agent operations are tracked consistently in the agent_activity_log table.
acceptanceCriteria: lib/services/agent-logger.ts exists with the following exports:

- logAgentAction(params: { orgId, agentType, actionType, contentId?, targetEntity?, targetId?, inputSummary?, outputSummary?, outcome, confidence?, durationMs?, tokensUsed?, costEstimate?, metadata? }): Promise<string> — inserts into agent_activity_log, returns the log entry id

- withAgentLogging<T>(params: { orgId, agentType, actionType, contentId?, targetEntity?, targetId?, inputSummary? }, fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> — higher-order wrapper that automatically logs start time, measures duration, catches errors, records outcome as 'success' or 'failure', stores error_message on failure, then rethrows

- getAgentActivity(params: { orgId, agentType?, actionType?, outcome?, limit?, offset?, startDate?, endDate? }): Promise<AgentActivityLog[]> — paginated query with optional filters, ordered by created_at DESC

- getAgentActionStats(params: { orgId, agentType?, startDate?, endDate? }): Promise<{ total: number, success: number, failure: number, skipped: number, avgDurationMs: number, totalTokens: number, totalCost: number }> — aggregate stats
AgentActivityLog interface exported matching agent_activity_log columns
Uses Supabase admin client with lazy init pattern
Typecheck passes

Example: withAgentLogging({ orgId: 'org_abc', agentType: 'curator', actionType: 'auto_categorize' }, async () => { /* categorize logic */ }) logs start time, executes the function, measures duration, and records outcome 'success' with durationMs in agent_activity_log
Edge case: If the wrapped function throws, withAgentLogging catches the error, logs outcome 'failure' with error_message, and rethrows the original error so the caller's error handling is preserved
Edge case: getAgentActionStats for an org with zero logged actions returns all-zero stats (total: 0, success: 0, avgDurationMs: 0, etc.), not null or error
stories.notes: System context: Every agent operation should call logAgentAction or use withAgentLogging wrapper. E04 Curator logs: auto_categorize, detect_duplicate, detect_stale, suggest_merge. E05 Gap Intelligence logs: analyze_gaps, detect_bus_factor. E07 Onboarding logs: generate_plan, track_engagement. E09 Digest logs: generate_digest. E11 Agent Dashboard reads via getAgentActivity and getAgentActionStats. E13 Usage Tracking aggregates tokensUsed and costEstimate from these logs. The withAgentLogging wrapper is the preferred pattern — it ensures actions are always logged even on failure.

stories.title: Create generate_metadata job handler
stories.description: As a user, I want my recordings to automatically get meaningful titles and descriptions so that I never see 'Recording 2026-02-11' in my library.
acceptanceCriteria: lib/workers/handlers/generate-metadata.ts exists with export async function handleGenerateMetadata(job: Job, progressCallback?: ProgressCallback): Promise<void>
Handler reads transcript text from transcripts table by content_id (from job.payload.recordingId)

Uses Google Gemini (via lazy-initialized GoogleGenerativeAI client, same pattern as docify-google.ts) with a prompt that generates: a concise title (max 80 chars, descriptive of content topic), a 1-2 sentence description summarizing the content, and up to 5 suggested tag names
Prompt instructs Gemini to avoid generic titles like 'Screen Recording' or 'Meeting Notes' — instead extract the actual topic

Updates content table: sets title (only if current title is null, empty, or matches auto-generated pattern like 'Recording YYYY-MM-DD' or 'Untitled'), sets description (only if current description is null or empty)
Stores suggested tags in job result metadata (does not auto-apply tags — that is E04 Curator's job)
Uses withAgentLogging wrapper from lib/services/agent-logger.ts with agentType: 'smart_processing', actionType: 'generate_metadata'
Error handling: if transcript not found, logs warning and completes without error; if Gemini call fails, retries via standard job retry mechanism
Typecheck passes
Example: Given a transcript about 'deploying a React app to AWS using Docker', Gemini generates title 'Deploying a React App to AWS with Docker' (not 'Screen Recording 2026-02-11' or 'Meeting Notes')
Edge case: If the content already has a user-edited title (not matching auto-generated patterns), the handler preserves the existing title and does not overwrite it
Edge case: If the transcript is extremely short (<50 characters), the handler still generates a title but notes low confidence in metadata
Edge case: If the Gemini API returns a rate limit error, the handler allows the standard job retry mechanism to re-queue the job
stories.notes: System context: This is the first visible 'agent' feature users experience. SG1 from the 10x analysis. The handler follows the same pattern as lib/workers/handlers/generate-summary.ts but focuses on title + description rather than full summary. Uses Gemini (not OpenAI) consistent with docify-google.ts. The suggested tags are stored in metadata for the Curator Agent (E04 US-017) to use later — we don't auto-tag here because auto-tagging requires checking existing tag patterns (Curator's job). The title-update guard (only if null/empty/auto-pattern) prevents overwriting user-edited titles.

Typecheck passes

acceptanceCriteria: app/(dashboard)/settings/organization/agents/page.tsx exists as a new org settings page
Page shows: global agent toggle (from org_agent_settings.global_agent_enabled), per-agent-type enable/disable toggles, and per-action permission tier selectors
Each agent type (curator, gap_intelligence, onboarding, digest, workflow_extraction) displayed as a collapsible section
Within each section: toggle to enable/disable the agent, and a list of its action types with dropdown selector for permission tier (Auto / Notify / Approve)
Changes save immediately via PATCH to /api/organizations/agent-settings and /api/organizations/agent-permissions API routes
Add 'Agents' link to the org settings sidebar navigation (below existing items like Security, Billing)
Shows description for each tier: Auto = 'Agent acts immediately', Notify = 'Agent acts and notifies you', Approve = 'Agent requests your approval first'
Visual indicator when agent is disabled (grayed out section with enable prompt)
Typecheck passes

Example: Admin navigates to Settings > Organization > Agents, sees the Curator section expanded with toggle ON, and action rows showing: 'Extract Concepts' = Auto, 'Suggest Tags' = Notify, 'Auto-Apply Tags' = Approve — each with a dropdown to change the tier

Edge case: Toggling the global_agent_enabled switch to OFF visually grays out all agent sections and shows a banner 'All agents are paused' — individual toggles are preserved but ineffective until global is re-enabled
Edge case: If an agent type has no configurable actions (edge case during early development), its section shows the enable/disable toggle but no action rows
Edge case: Changes save immediately on dropdown change with optimistic UI update and a subtle toast confirmation — failed saves revert the dropdown and show an error toast
stories.notes: System context: The UI for controlling agent behavior. Makes agents visible and controllable (anti-pattern #5 from 10x analysis: 'agents in the background are invisible by default'). The settings page is the trust-building interface — orgs need to feel in control before enabling autonomous agents. Placed in org settings because agent configuration is an org-level decision (not per-user). Uses the same settings layout pattern as existing org settings pages.

stories.title: Implement approval queue for Tier 3 agent actions
stories.description: As an org admin, I want to see pending agent actions that require my approval so that I can approve or reject them before the agent acts.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration creates `agent_approval_queue` table via Supabase MCP with columns: id (uuid PK DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()), org_id (text NOT NULL), agent_type (text NOT NULL), action_type (text NOT NULL), content_id (uuid REFERENCES content(id) ON DELETE CASCADE), description (text NOT NULL), proposed_action (jsonb NOT NULL), status (text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK pending|approved|rejected|expired), reviewed_by (text), reviewed_at (timestamptz), rejection_reason (text), expires_at (timestamptz DEFAULT now() + interval '7 days'), created_at (timestamptz DEFAULT now())
Indexes: idx_approval_queue_org_status (org_id, status) WHERE status = 'pending', idx_approval_queue_expires (expires_at) WHERE status = 'pending'
API routes: GET /api/organizations/agent-approvals (list pending), PATCH /api/organizations/agent-approvals/[id] (approve/reject)
lib/services/agent-permissions.ts adds requestApproval(params): Promise<string> function that inserts into approval queue and returns approval ID
Agent handlers call requestApproval when checkPermission returns 'approve', then stop processing that action (do not proceed until approved)
Expired approvals (>7 days) auto-transition to 'expired' status
Approval queue UI accessible from the agent settings page (US-027) as a tab or linked section
Typecheck passes

Example: Curator detects a near-duplicate and checkPermission returns 'approve' for 'merge_content'. It calls requestApproval({ orgId, agentType: 'curator', actionType: 'merge_content', contentId, description: 'Merge duplicate recordings about React deployment', proposedAction: { type: 'merge', sourceIds: [...] } }). The approval appears in the queue with status 'pending' and 7-day expiry.
Edge case: An approval that reaches its 7-day expiry transitions to 'expired' status automatically — the agent does not proceed with the action
Edge case: Rejecting an approval stores the rejection_reason and reviewed_by — the agent receives the rejection and logs it in agent_activity_log with outcome 'skipped'

Edge case: If the same agent requests approval for the same content_id and action_type while a pending approval already exists, the system returns the existing approval ID instead of creating a duplicate
stories.notes: System context: Completes the authorization framework. Tier 3 actions (like auto-applying tags or merging content) require explicit approval before execution. The approval queue is the mechanism. 7-day expiry prevents stale approvals from piling up. The agent handlers need to be designed to be resumable: when an approval comes in, the system should be able to execute the approved action. This is a key enterprise requirement — organizations won't enable autonomous agents without this guardrail.

stories.title: Add agent action cost estimation
stories.description: As an org admin, I want to see estimated costs before approving agent actions so that I can make informed decisions about agent operations.
acceptanceCriteria: lib/services/agent-cost-estimator.ts exports estimateActionCost(agentType, actionType, metadata?): Promise<{ estimatedTokens: number, estimatedCostUsd: number, breakdown: string }>

Cost estimates based on the action type: generate_metadata (~500 tokens, ~$0.001), auto_categorize (~1000 tokens, ~$0.002), detect_duplicate (~200 tokens, ~$0.0005), analyze_gaps (~2000 tokens, ~$0.004), generate_onboarding_plan (~3000 tokens, ~$0.006)
Uses the same cost model as lib/services/processing-decision-engine.ts (if it exists) for consistency
Cost estimate included in approval queue entries (proposed_action.estimatedCost)
Cost displayed in the approval queue UI next to each pending action
Aggregate cost display on agent settings page: 'Estimated monthly agent cost: $X.XX based on current content volume'
Typecheck passes

Example: estimateActionCost('curator', 'auto_categorize') returns { estimatedTokens: 1000, estimatedCostUsd: 0.002, breakdown: '~500 input tokens (concept context) + ~500 output tokens (tag suggestions) using Gemini Flash' }
Edge case: estimateActionCost for an unknown action_type returns a conservative high estimate with breakdown 'Unknown action type — using maximum estimate' rather than erroring
Edge case: The monthly cost estimate on the agent settings page handles orgs with zero content gracefully, showing '$0.00 estimated' instead of NaN or division-by-zero
stories.notes: System context: Addresses anti-pattern #4 from 10x analysis: 'Ignoring Cost Economics.' The processing-decision-engine.ts already handles cost-aware processing decisions — this extends that pattern to agent operations. Cost transparency builds trust and helps orgs budget for agent features. The estimates don't need to be precise — directionally correct is sufficient. This data also feeds into E13 (Pricing & Usage Tracking).

stories.title: Create agent_onboarding_plans table migration
stories.description: As a developer, I want an agent_onboarding_plans table so that personalized learning paths for new team members can be stored and tracked.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration creates `agent_onboarding_plans` table via Supabase MCP with columns: id (uuid PK DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()), org_id (text NOT NULL), user_id (text NOT NULL), user_name (text), user_role (text), plan_status (text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active' CHECK active|completed|paused|expired), learning_path (jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'), total_items (integer DEFAULT 0), completed_items (integer DEFAULT 0), engagement_data (jsonb DEFAULT '{}'), generated_by (text DEFAULT 'agent'), reviewed_by (text), notes (text), created_at (timestamptz DEFAULT now()), updated_at (timestamptz DEFAULT now())

learning_path JSONB structure: array of { contentId: string, title: string, contentType: string, reason: string, order: number, completed: boolean, completedAt: string | null, estimatedMinutes: number }
Indexes: idx_onboarding_plans_org (org_id), idx_onboarding_plans_user (user_id), idx_onboarding_plans_org_status (org_id, plan_status)
RLS: SELECT by plan owner (user_id) and org admins, INSERT/UPDATE via service role
Typecheck passes

Example: INSERT INTO agent_onboarding_plans (org_id, user_id, user_name, user_role, learning_path, total_items) VALUES ('org_abc', 'user_new', 'Alice Johnson', 'backend_engineer', '[{"contentId":"c1","title":"Local Dev Setup","order":1,...}]', 10) succeeds with plan_status 'active'
Edge case: Attempting to set plan_status to an invalid value (e.g., 'cancelled') is rejected by the CHECK constraint
Edge case: A user can have multiple plans (e.g., if they switch roles) — the table allows multiple rows per user_id with different plan_status values
stories.notes: System context: Storage for the Onboarding Agent (M3 from 10x analysis). The learning_path is a JSON array of content items ordered for optimal learning. The engagement_data tracks behavioral signals (what was viewed, time spent, questions asked) for path refinement (US-039). The reason field in each learning path item explains why this content was included ('Covers deployment process — essential for backend engineers'). This enables the adaptive refinement in later stories.

stories.title: Implement generate-onboarding-plan job handler
stories.description: As a developer, I want a job handler that generates personalized learning paths for new team members using the knowledge graph and content library.
acceptanceCriteria: lib/workers/handlers/generate-onboarding-plan.ts exists with export async function handleGenerateOnboardingPlan(job: Job, progressCallback?: ProgressCallback): Promise<void>
Job payload: { orgId, userId, userName?, userRole? }
Handler checks isAgentEnabled(orgId, 'onboarding')

Learning path generation: (1) Query knowledge_concepts for the org ordered by mention count DESC to find core topics, (2) Filter concepts relevant to userRole if provided (use Gemini to match role to concept relevance), (3) Find content items covering those concepts via concept_mentions JOIN content, ordered by freshness and quality, (4) Use Gemini to sequence content into optimal learning order with reasons
Limits path to 10-20 items (configurable) to avoid overwhelming new members
Inserts learning path into agent_onboarding_plans table
Includes estimatedMinutes for each item (based on content duration for recordings/videos, word count for documents)
Logs via withAgentLogging with agentType: 'onboarding', actionType: 'generate_plan'
Add 'generate_onboarding_plan' to JobType and register in JOB_HANDLERS with priority NORMAL
Typecheck passes

Example: For a new backend engineer joining an org with 200 content items, the handler identifies core concepts (Kubernetes, CI/CD, API Design) from knowledge_concepts, filters for backend-relevant content via Gemini, and produces a 15-item learning path starting with 'Local Development Setup' and ending with 'Production Deployment Runbook'

Edge case: For an org with fewer than 5 content items, the handler generates a shorter path using all available content and adds a note in plan metadata: 'Limited content available — path may be incomplete'
Edge case: If userRole is not provided, the handler generates a general learning path without role-based filtering — covering the org's top concepts broadly
Edge case: If Gemini sequencing fails (API error), the handler falls back to ordering by concept mention count DESC (most-referenced content first)
stories.notes: System context: Core of the Onboarding Agent (M3). Uses the knowledge graph to understand what concepts are most important in the org, then maps those to content items. The role-based filtering is important: a backend engineer needs different content than a designer. Gemini does the heavy lifting of sequencing — it understands that 'setup local dev environment' should come before 'deploying to production.' The 10-20 item limit prevents information overload.

Progress bar at top showing completed_items / total_items
Each item links to /library/{contentId} when clicked
Completed items are visually distinct (strikethrough or dimmed) but still accessible
Mark item as complete calls PATCH /api/onboarding/progress with contentId
API route app/api/onboarding/progress/route.ts updates the learning_path item's completed field and increments completed_items
Show 'No onboarding plan yet' if no active plan exists, with option for admin to trigger generation
Add 'Onboarding' link to sidebar navigation (conditionally shown when user has an active plan)
Typecheck passes

Example: New team member Alice visits /onboarding and sees: progress bar '3/15 completed', a checklist with items like '1. Local Dev Setup (video, 8 min) — Covers setting up the development environment. Essential for all engineers.' with a checkbox and link
Edge case: If no active onboarding plan exists for the current user, the page shows 'No onboarding plan yet' with a message for admins to trigger generation
Edge case: Marking the last incomplete item as complete transitions plan_status from 'active' to 'completed' automatically
Edge case: Completed items remain visible (dimmed/strikethrough) and clickable so users can revisit content — they are not hidden or removed from the list
stories.notes: System context: The user-facing output of the Onboarding Agent. This page is what new team members see when they join. The checklist format is deliberately simple — it should feel like a guided tour, not a course. The reason field helps new members understand why each piece of content matters. Progress tracking (completed_items) feeds into US-037 (engagement tracking) and US-039 (adaptive refinement).

stories.title: Detect new org members via Clerk webhooks and auto-trigger plan generation
stories.description: As an org admin, I want the Onboarding Agent to automatically detect when new members join and generate a learning path without manual intervention.
acceptanceCriteria: Update existing Clerk webhook handler (app/api/webhooks/ or similar) to detect organizationMembership.created events

When a new member joins an org: check isAgentEnabled(orgId, 'onboarding'), if enabled create a generate_onboarding_plan job with the new member's userId, userName, and role (from Clerk membership metadata)
If Clerk webhook handler doesn't exist, create app/api/webhooks/clerk/route.ts with POST handler that validates webhook signature (svix) and routes events
Handle the case where the same user is added and removed repeatedly (dedupe_key: `onboarding_plan:${orgId}:${userId}`)
Log the detection via withAgentLogging with agentType: 'onboarding', actionType: 'detect_new_member'
Typecheck passes

Example: When user_alice is added to org_abc via Clerk dashboard, the organizationMembership.created webhook fires, the handler verifies onboarding is enabled, and creates a generate_onboarding_plan job with payload { orgId: 'org_abc', userId: 'user_alice', userName: 'Alice Johnson', userRole: 'engineer' }
Edge case: If the same user is removed and re-added to the org, the dedupe_key (onboarding_plan:org_abc:user_alice) prevents generating a duplicate plan — the existing plan (if any) remains
Edge case: If the Clerk webhook signature validation fails (invalid svix signature), the handler returns 401 and does not process the event
Edge case: If the org has onboarding disabled (isAgentEnabled returns false), the webhook handler logs the new member detection but does not create a job
stories.notes: System context: The trigger mechanism for the Onboarding Agent. Clerk's organization webhooks fire when members are added. The webhook-to-job pipeline follows the existing pattern in lib/workers/handlers/process-webhook.ts. The dedupe key prevents generating multiple plans if someone is added, removed, and re-added. This is the first truly 'proactive' agent behavior — it acts without any user trigger.

stories.title: Implement engagement tracking and adaptive path refinement
stories.description: As a developer, I want to track onboarding engagement and refine future learning paths based on behavioral data from previous onboardings.
acceptanceCriteria: Track engagement signals on onboarding content: content viewed (time on page), content completed (checkbox), questions asked via ContentChatWidget (if US-012 is done), search queries from the new member
Store engagement data in agent_onboarding_plans.engagement_data as JSON: { viewedContent: [{ contentId, viewedAt, durationSec }], searchQueries: string[], chatQuestions: string[] }

After an onboarding plan is completed (all items checked), use Gemini to analyze engagement: which items were skipped or spent little time on, which generated questions, what was searched but not in the plan
Store analysis in agent memory: storeMemory with key 'onboarding_analysis:{orgId}:{role}' containing insights for improving future plans

Next time a plan is generated for the same role (in US-031), recall this memory to adjust: remove items that were consistently skipped, add topics that were searched but missing, reorder based on actual engagement patterns
Typecheck passes

Example: After 10 backend engineers complete onboarding, the agent memory contains insights like 'onboarding_analysis:org_abc:backend_engineer' → 'Items about local dev setup are always completed first and quickly. Items about legacy migration are frequently skipped. Engineers often search for API documentation not in the plan.' Future plans for backend engineers auto-include API docs and deprioritize legacy migration.
Edge case: If an onboarding plan has only 1 completed item out of 15 (user abandoned), the analysis still runs but flags low engagement and stores that insight with lower importance (0.5)
Edge case: Engagement tracking gracefully handles the absence of ContentChatWidget (US-012 may not be implemented) — chat questions are simply empty in that case
Edge case: The first onboarding for a role has no prior memory to refine from — the plan is generated purely from the knowledge graph without behavioral adjustments
stories.notes: System context: The adaptive refinement loop that makes the Onboarding Agent compound in value. After 10 onboardings, the agent knows exactly what new backend engineers need because it's seen which content was useful and which was skipped. This uses the agent memory system (US-004) to persist insights across onboarding cycles. The engagement tracking is lightweight — we're not building a full LMS, just capturing signals that improve future plans.

stories.title: Create agent_feedback table and feedback UI components
stories.description: As a user, I want to give feedback on agent actions (thumbs up/down, corrections) so that agents improve over time based on my input.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration creates `agent_feedback` table via Supabase MCP with columns: id (uuid PK DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()), org_id (text NOT NULL), user_id (text NOT NULL), agent_activity_log_id (uuid REFERENCES agent_activity_log(id) ON DELETE CASCADE), feedback_type (text NOT NULL CHECK thumbs_up|thumbs_down|correction|rating), score (integer CHECK score >= 1 AND score <= 5), correction_value (text), comment (text), metadata (jsonb DEFAULT '{}'), created_at (timestamptz DEFAULT now())
Indexes: idx_agent_feedback_activity (agent_activity_log_id), idx_agent_feedback_org (org_id, created_at DESC)
RLS: INSERT by org members, SELECT by org members (see own feedback) and admins (see all)
API route app/api/agent-feedback/route.ts with POST (submit feedback) validating auth and orgId
app/components/agent/AgentFeedbackButtons.tsx Client Component with thumbs up/down buttons, calls POST /api/agent-feedback
Props: activityLogId (string), onFeedback? (callback)
Buttons show filled state after user provides feedback (prevent duplicate feedback)
Compact size suitable for inline use (next to agent-generated titles, tags, suggestions)
Typecheck passes

Example: User sees a Curator-generated title suggestion with thumbs up/down buttons inline. Clicking thumbs down calls POST /api/agent-feedback with { agent_activity_log_id: 'log_xyz', feedback_type: 'thumbs_down' } and the button fills to indicate feedback was recorded.

Edge case: Submitting feedback twice for the same agent_activity_log_id by the same user does not create a duplicate — the second submission updates the existing feedback record or is silently ignored
Edge case: The AgentFeedbackButtons component handles a missing or invalid activityLogId gracefully by disabling the buttons and not sending API calls
Edge case: Feedback submitted by a user not in the org associated with the agent_activity_log entry returns 403 Forbidden
stories.notes: System context: MD4 from 10x analysis. The feedback loop is essential: 'The difference between an agent that improves and one that stays static.' The AgentFeedbackButtons component will be placed next to auto-generated titles (US-007), suggested tags (US-016), and related content suggestions (US-009). The agent_activity_log_id links feedback directly to the specific agent action, enabling per-action learning. US-043 integrates this feedback into agent memory.

stories.title: Add concept correction UI and RAG response rating
stories.description: As a user, I want to correct extracted concepts and rate RAG assistant responses so that the knowledge graph and search improve from my expertise.
acceptanceCriteria: app/components/knowledge/ConceptCorrection.tsx Client Component for editing extracted concepts: allows renaming, changing type, merging with another concept, or marking as incorrect
Concept corrections call PATCH /api/concepts/[id] route that updates knowledge_concepts and logs a correction in agent_feedback
API route app/api/concepts/[id]/route.ts with PATCH (update concept fields), scoped by orgId
app/components/chat/ResponseRating.tsx Client Component with 1-5 star rating for RAG responses, plus optional text comment
Rating component integrates into the existing chat/assistant interface (rendered after each assistant response)
Ratings stored via POST /api/agent-feedback with feedback_type: 'rating', metadata: { responseId, query, responseSnippet }
Typecheck passes

Example: On the knowledge graph page, user sees concept 'ReactJS' and clicks edit. They rename it to 'React' and set type to 'framework'. The PATCH /api/concepts/abc updates the knowledge_concepts row and logs a correction in agent_feedback.

Example: After an assistant response about deployment, user rates it 2/5 stars and comments 'Answer was about the wrong deployment pipeline.' This is stored as agent_feedback with feedback_type 'rating', score 2, and the comment.
Edge case: Merging two concepts (e.g., 'ReactJS' into 'React') updates all concept_mentions referencing the old concept_id to point to the merged concept — no orphan mentions remain
Edge case: Rating a response that has already been rated by the same user updates the existing rating rather than creating a duplicate
stories.notes: System context: Two specialized feedback mechanisms. Concept corrections directly improve the knowledge graph — if a user renames a concept or merges duplicates, that's high-signal data. RAG response ratings provide training signal for search quality improvement. Both feed into the feedback integration story (US-037). The concept correction UI should be accessible from the knowledge graph page and from content detail pages where concepts are displayed.

stories.title: Integrate feedback into agent memory for behavior refinement
stories.description: As a developer, I want agent feedback to automatically feed into agent memory so that agents learn from user corrections and improve over time.
acceptanceCriteria: lib/services/feedback-processor.ts exports processFeedback(feedbackId: string): Promise<void>
When thumbs_down feedback received on auto-categorize action: store memory 'negative_feedback:categorize:{contentId}' with the bad suggestion, so future categorization avoids similar mistakes
When concept correction received: store memory 'concept_correction:{conceptId}' with before/after, so concept extraction learns org-specific terminology
When RAG response rated low (<=2): store memory 'low_rated_query:{queryHash}' with the query and response, so future RAG retrieval can adjust
When thumbs_up received: store memory with high importance (0.9) to reinforce good patterns
processFeedback called automatically after feedback is submitted (triggered in the POST /api/agent-feedback route handler)
Uses storeMemory from lib/services/agent-memory.ts with appropriate importance scores (negative feedback: 0.8, positive: 0.9, corrections: 0.95)
Typecheck passes

Example: User gives thumbs_down on a Curator auto-categorize action that suggested tag 'backend' for a frontend tutorial. processFeedback stores memory 'negative_feedback:categorize:content_xyz' → 'Incorrectly suggested backend tag for frontend React tutorial. Avoid backend tags for React/UI content.' with importance 0.8. Next time the Curator processes similar React content, searchMemory finds this signal and avoids suggesting 'backend'.

Edge case: If storeMemory fails during feedback processing (e.g., embedding generation timeout), the feedback is still saved in agent_feedback — the memory integration is retried on next processFeedback call

Edge case: Multiple negative feedbacks on the same pattern (e.g., repeatedly bad categorization of frontend content) increase the memory importance up to a cap of 0.99 rather than creating duplicate memories
stories.notes: System context: Closes the feedback loop. Agent memory is the bridge between user feedback and agent behavior. When the Curator suggests bad tags and gets thumbs down, it stores that as a negative signal. Next time it categorizes similar content, searchMemory finds the negative signal and adjusts. Importance scores ensure corrections (0.95) are weighted more heavily than general positive/negative signals. This is the mechanism that makes agents compound in value over time.

stories.title: Implement generate_weekly_digest job handler
stories.description: As a developer, I want a weekly digest handler that generates a comprehensive knowledge report for each org covering new content, trending concepts, and knowledge health.
acceptanceCriteria: lib/workers/handlers/generate-weekly-digest.ts exists with export async function handleGenerateWeeklyDigest(job: Job, progressCallback?: ProgressCallback): Promise<void>
Job payload: { orgId }

Collects data for the past 7 days: new content items (count and titles), new concepts extracted (count and top 10 by mention count), knowledge gaps detected (new and still open), curator actions (duplicates found, stale content detected), search activity (total searches, top queries, failed searches), agent activity summary (actions taken, success rate)
Uses Gemini to generate a natural-language summary paragraph highlighting key insights

Stores digest in agent_activity_log with action_type: 'weekly_digest', output_summary containing the full digest as JSON: { period: { start, end }, summary: string, stats: { ... }, highlights: string[], gaps: string[] }
Logs via withAgentLogging with agentType: 'digest', actionType: 'generate_digest'
Add 'generate_weekly_digest' to JobType and register in JOB_HANDLERS with priority LOW
Typecheck passes

Example: Weekly digest for org_abc contains: summary 'Your team added 12 recordings this week, primarily about Kubernetes migration. 3 new concepts were extracted. Knowledge health score improved from 65 to 72.', stats { contentAdded: 12, conceptsExtracted: 3, healthScore: 72, searches: 145, failedSearches: 8 }, highlights: ['Kubernetes migration is trending — 8 new recordings this week', 'Knowledge gap detected: no content about staging environment setup']

stories.notes: System context: SG4 from the 10x analysis: 'First truly proactive agent feature users interact with. Arrives without being asked.' The digest aggregates data from multiple systems: content table, knowledge_concepts, knowledge_gaps (if E05 done), agent_activity_log, search monitoring. Gemini generates the natural-language summary so it reads like a colleague's update, not a data dump. The JSON structure allows both in-app rendering (US-041) and email (US-040).

At hard stop (100%): agent operations return early with a 'credit limit exceeded' message instead of processing
checkUsageLimits called at the start of withAgentLogging before executing the wrapped function
Usage alert banner displayed on agent settings and usage pages when warning threshold reached
Typecheck passes

Example: At 80% credit usage (800/1000 Pro credits), checkUsageLimits returns { level: 'warning', currentUsage: 800, limit: 1000, message: 'You have used 80% of your monthly AI credits.' } and a yellow banner appears on the agent settings page

Edge case: At 100% credit limit (hard stop), agent operations called via withAgentLogging return early without executing the wrapped function, logging outcome 'skipped' with reason 'credit limit exceeded' — no API costs are incurred
Edge case: The credit limit check in withAgentLogging adds minimal latency (<5ms) by caching the current usage count in Redis with a 60-second TTL rather than querying the database on every action
Edge case: If the Redis cache is unavailable, the check falls back to a direct database query rather than blocking all agent operations — availability is prioritized over strict rate accuracy
